author: tyresia2
quote:
Extremely boring game, filled with not-so-veiled feminist propaganda. Just as everyone expected, all women are strong, wise, powerful, resilient and even physically superior to men in most instances. 

Lucia is bossy and obnoxious, constantly starved for attention and borderline psychotic, but the game somehow forces you to like her. Can you complete the game without romancing her? Sure you can, but you'll be soft-locked out of most of the narrative if you do. So you're stuck with an extremely unbalanced girlfriend simulator where a spoiled, unsufferable woman constantly takes the scene, leaving the bumbling protagonist to lie in shadows. I mean, for a game called "Grand Theft Auto", it's quite symbolic how most of the time she's the one behind the wheel during chases and action sequences. 

I spent the entire game praying Lucia would be incarcerated again, this time for good. And we're supposed to bond with her.

Besides that, the gameplay is tear-inducingly boring. We waited 13 years for a modern reskin of Red Dead Redemption 2, minus the charming characters, the charismatic main charachter, the breath-taking setting, the compelling story, and the powerful script. All we've got is an "open world" that leaves you with very little to do, lots and lots of invisible walls and limited content, and endless indoctrination hidden nearly everywhere. We were expecting action, destruction, freedom, silly comedy, social criticism, and explosions. What we've got is a wannabe The Sims with some foid-written misandrist romance.

My best advice is to avoid paying $100 for an HR struggling session padded with fake gameplay and a daily chores simulator. Unless you really like the idea of experiencing the pain of dealing with a toxic woman. Like the ones who wrote the script of this overpriced dumpster fire.
